<!-- pr-reviewer: 1728ce6516e1ab7ad461c1e1ed8da3621e364d49 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** (High-tier review: stock/toolpath work under the safety floor.)

## What looks good
- Each new seam op is the old `Dexel` call on the column arm, with no change to bounds or index math (`backend_edit.rs:41-48`, `:61-65`, `:80-92`):
  - `subtract_flat` calls `Dexel::subtract` and `cut_chord` calls `Dexel::cut_chord`, so empty-column and degenerate cases come from the same code as before.
  - `set_tops` visits the columns in the same row-major order with `k = ix + iy*nx`, and skips a write only when the new top has the same bits as the current one.
- Rewritten call sites match the old behaviour:
  - `sim_of` writes `pt` only where `pt > top`, so NaN and equal heights are untouched, as before.
  - `stock_for` clears exactly the columns outside the region.
  - `Stock::measure` builds the part surface from the same `x0, y0, cell, nx, ny` that `run_rest` used.
  - `part_of` reads the origin from `Columns::origin()` and the lattice from `cell/nx/ny`, which are the same fields.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the non-test code touched. The posed-move refusal runs before any column is touched. New cuts return `Result` where they can refuse.
- No golden or snapshot file changed. No `build.rs`, `.github`, scripts, process files or dependency changes. The `Columns::to_stock` clone is the one `run_rest` already made.
- `docs/decisions/587-motion-onto-stock.md` is present. The body has `Changelog: none`, `Effort: high` and `Fixes #587`. The new module has a provenance line.
- `#[test]` count: only one test is added (`stock_seam::motion_names_no_dexel_outside_tests`). The edited tests keep their counts, and `engagement_on` is pinned bit for bit against the direct read.
- File sizes: the new `backend_edit.rs` has 102 lines. The largest touched files are `ladder.rs` (360) and `quality/mod.rs` (358). `descent.rs` is 423 lines but this PR does not touch it.
- `rg Dexel` in `crates/motion/src` outside `tests.rs` finds no code hits; the scan test passes.

## Local results (merged with upstream/main: already up to date, no conflicts)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-app --test stock_engine_agreement` (release, `--include-ignored`) | 3 passed |
| camcraft-sim, all suites | 378 passed, 0 failed |
| camcraft-motion: lib, adaptive_hsm, machining3d, multiaxis, multiaxis_avoid, multiaxis_rough, one_descent, pocket3d_hsm, posed_subtract, stock_seam, engagement_3d, optimal_load, level_links, rotary_adaptive, rotary | 254 passed, 0 failed |
| camcraft-app `golden_cl` | 24 passed |
| camcraft-app `pocket3d_hsm` | 6 passed |
| camcraft-app `center_cut_multiaxis` | 1 passed, 1 ignored |
| camcraft-app `solid_law` | 4 passed |
| clippy `-D warnings`, camcraft-sim + camcraft-motion + camcraft-app, all targets | clean |

I skipped the slow `finish3d`, `pivot5d` and `flow` suites because the diff does not touch them. The author reports them green on the Linux batch gate.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
- `Columns::col` refuses a non-finite point, where `Dexel::col` maps NaN to column 0. Motion now reads stricter on non-finite input. This is safe and cannot change a finite result.
- `subtract_flat` now refuses a posed move on its own, and `optimize_feed` calls it directly. Before, `optimize_feed` did not refuse a posed move. This can only refuse more, never cut wrongly, and the goldens show no case that hits it.
- Field arm of `cut_chord` (`backend_edit.rs:61-72`), for 6/6: no caller reaches it yet. It sweeps the flat tool along the chord. `Dexel::cut_chord` instead removes everything above the chord's lowest Z at each touched cell. Check the two agree on tilted chords before 6/6 switches the backend. It would be worth adding a field-arm test for `cut_chord` and `subtract_flat` then.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
